description: 12 sample suite definitions, 27 cases total. POST each payload to /eval-suites. Suites 10-12 each contain one positive control and two intentional failures. Expected statuses are testing intentions; live model behavior can vary.

cases.name: addition
cases.input: Use the add tool to calculate 17 + 25. State the result.
cases.criteria: States that 17 + 25 equals 42.

cases.name: subtraction
cases.input: Use the subtract tool to calculate 100 - 37. State the result.
cases.criteria: States that 100 - 37 equals 63.

suites.description: Strict tool-only checks; no judge calls.

cases.name: multiply
cases.input: Use only the multiply tool to calculate 12 times 8.

cases.name: divide
cases.input: Use only the divide tool to calculate 144 divided by 12.

suites.description: Correctness checks for less trivial numeric inputs.

cases.name: decimal_sum
cases.input: Use the add tool to calculate 7.5 + 2.25.
cases.criteria: States that the result is 9.75.

cases.name: negative_sum
cases.input: Use the add tool to calculate -8 + 3.
cases.criteria: States that the result is -5.

suites.description: Two numeric judge scores plus tool checks.

cases.name: power
cases.input: Use exponentiate to calculate 2 to the power of 10. Briefly explain the result.
cases.criteria: Gives 1024 as the result and clearly explains that 2 is raised to the tenth power.

cases.name: root
cases.input: Use square_root to calculate the square root of 81. Briefly explain the result.
cases.criteria: Gives the principal square root as 9 and explains that 9 squared equals 81.

cases.name: zero_factorial
cases.input: Use the factorial tool to calculate 0 factorial.
cases.criteria: Correctly states that 0 factorial equals 1.

cases.name: one_not_prime
cases.input: Call is_prime with n=1 and explain the result.
cases.criteria: Correctly states that 1 is not prime because it has only one positive divisor.

suites.description: Each case requires more than one calculator tool.

cases.name: sum_then_multiply
cases.input: Use add to calculate 2 + 3, then multiply that result by 4 using multiply. State the final result.
cases.criteria: States that (2 + 3) times 4 equals 20.

cases.name: average
cases.input: Use add to sum 10 and 20, then use divide to divide the sum by 2. State the average.
cases.criteria: States that the average of 10 and 20 is 15.

suites.description: Everyday percentage calculations with combined checks.

cases.name: percentage
cases.input: Use multiply to calculate 20 percent of 200, by multiplying 200 by 0.2.
cases.criteria: States that 20 percent of 200 is 40.

cases.name: tip
cases.input: Use multiply to calculate a 12.5 percent tip on 80, by multiplying 80 by 0.125.
cases.criteria: States that the tip is 10.

suites.description: Judge-only cases; expected tool calls should be left blank.

cases.name: prime_definition
cases.input: In two sentences explain what a prime number is. No calculations are needed.
cases.criteria: Explains that a prime is an integer greater than 1 with exactly two distinct positive divisors, 1 and itself.

cases.name: zero_division
cases.input: Explain why dividing by zero is undefined. Do not use a numeric example or calculator.
cases.criteria: Explains that division by zero is undefined and does not present infinity as its arithmetic result.

suites.description: Judge-only cases with a passing score of 8/10.

cases.name: fraction_definition
cases.input: Explain numerator and denominator in two short sentences, without numerical examples.
cases.criteria: Clearly distinguishes the numerator as the count of selected equal parts and the denominator as the number of equal parts in a whole.

cases.name: area_vs_perimeter
cases.input: In two sentences explain the difference between area and perimeter. No calculations are needed.
cases.criteria: Clearly describes area as the amount of surface inside a shape and perimeter as the length around its boundary.

suites.description: One positive control, one wrong tool expectation, and one missing required tool.

cases.name: control
cases.input: Use only add to calculate 2 + 2.

cases.name: wrong_tool_expectation
cases.input: Use only add to calculate 2 + 2. Do not call subtract.

cases.name: missing_second_tool
cases.input: Use only add to calculate 6 + 4. Do not call multiply.

suites.description: One positive control, one binary judge failure, and one numeric score below the passing threshold.

cases.name: control
cases.input: Use add to calculate 2 + 2 and state the result.
cases.criteria: Correctly states that 2 + 2 equals 4.

cases.name: wrong_answer_expectation
cases.input: Use add to calculate 2 + 2. State only the actual result returned by the tool.
cases.criteria: The response explicitly states that the result of 2 + 2 is 5.

cases.name: numeric_score_below_threshold
cases.input: Use multiply to calculate 3 times 3. State only the actual result returned by the tool.
cases.criteria: The response explicitly states that 3 times 3 equals 12. Score 1 if it instead gives 9; score 10 only if it explicitly gives 12.

suites.description: One positive control, one forbidden additional tool, and one case failing both judge and tool checks.

cases.name: additional_tools_allowed
cases.input: Call add to calculate 2 + 3, then call multiply to multiply the result by 4. State the final result.

cases.name: additional_tools_forbidden
cases.input: Call add to calculate 2 + 3, then call multiply to multiply the result by 4. State the final result.

cases.name: judge_and_tool_failure
cases.input: Use only subtract to calculate 10 - 3. State only the actual result returned by the tool.
cases.criteria: The response explicitly states that the result is 99.
